The NCAA released updated details on its proposed age-based eligibility model, changing when an athlete’s five-year eligibility clock begins. Protect College Sports Act of 2026: The Senate Bill That Could Reshape Eligibility, Transfers & NIL

Keith Mondillo says while most families focus on the NCAA’s “five-for-five” age-based eligibility debate, the bigger development is the bipartisan Protect College Sports Act of 2026 moving through the U.S. Senate, which could federally codify eligibility (a five-year window starting at age 19 or high school graduation), affect transfers, NIL oversight, roster structure, and recruiting rules. He highlights the June 3 Senate Commerce Committee hearing featuring Nick Saban, Notre Dame AD Pete Bevilacqua, WVU President Emeritus Gordon Gee, Pac-12 Commissioner Teresa Gould, and Utah athlete Lance Holsclaw, summarizing warnings about NIL becoming pay-for-play, massive roster NIL commitments, and threats to women’s and Olympic sports. Mondillo explains ripple effects for Division II/III recruiting stability and urges families to keep recruiting outreach active, understand division options, and improve coach communication while the bill advances.
